spike_verdict: The core tension is carried cleanly by the evidence: F19 (Town Planning Commission called the site 'a favourite beauty spot') and F21 (soldiers' camp occupied the present parking lot) directly support the spike and subtitle as written — no overstatement in the SPIKE hero text itself.

blocking.where: overview.mdx, paragraph 2 ('Ferguson Point itself has a history...')
blocking.claim: "A World War II coastal gun battery once stood where the beach's own parking lot now sits, built over the objections of Vancouver's own planning commission..."
blocking.problem: This conflates the gun battery (guns/emplacements) with the soldiers' camp. Per F21, it was the soldiers' CAMP — not the guns — that occupied the ground now used as the parking lot; the battery itself sat on Ferguson Point's headland. Every other surface gets this right: history.mdx says 'A soldiers' camp went up alongside the guns, on the ground that is now Third Beach's parking lot,' and showcase.json's TEAHOUSE zone entry says the parking lot was 'built on the footprint of the WWII battery's soldiers' camp' (not the guns). Only this sentence in overview.mdx swaps 'soldiers' camp' for 'gun battery,' misstating what physically stood where the parking lot now is.
blocking.evidence: F21 (vancouvergunners.ca): "a soldiers' camp occupied the present third beach parking lot." Contrast history.mdx: "A soldiers' camp went up alongside the guns, on the ground that is now Third Beach's parking lot."
blocking.fix: Change to: "A World War II soldiers' camp tied to a coastal gun battery once stood where the beach's own parking lot now sits, the battery itself built over the objections of Vancouver's own planning commission..."

blocking.where: overview.mdx, final paragraph before the closing summary ('It has also drawn safety scrutiny of its own, covered in full on the [history spoke](/beaches/third-beach-1/history) alongside the site's military past.')
blocking.claim: The drum circle's safety scrutiny (the 2022 near-drowning, lifeguard pull, fencing, police patrols) is 'covered in full on the history spoke.'
blocking.problem: history.mdx (the history spoke) does not cover the drum circle or the near-drowning incident at all. Its content is entirely about the 1914/1938-45 gun battery and the Siwash Rock renaming dispute; the drum circle is mentioned only once, in passing, as an amenity ('a Tuesday drum circle') in the closing summary paragraph — with zero safety detail. A reader following this link expecting the near-drowning story will not find it there.
blocking.evidence: history.mdx sections are: 'A first battery nobody remembers, 1914'; '"A favourite beauty spot," 1938'; 'Stand-down and a slow reclamation, 1945-1948'; 'A second, quieter argument over naming' (Siwash Rock); 'What the history actually explains.' None discuss F31/F32 (the near-drowning, lifeguards pulled, fencing, police patrols) — that content exists only in showcase.json's honest_reckoning_note/spike_explainer and travel.mdx's Safety section.
blocking.fix: Either remove the cross-reference claim ('It has also drawn safety scrutiny of its own — see Safety, below/travel guide' pointing to travel.mdx instead), or actually add the near-drowning/fencing/lifeguard-pull content to history.mdx if the history spoke is meant to carry it.

blocking.where: travel.mdx, opening line and Costs section ('there is no direct road onto the sand itself, and no road-distance or transit-route figures...' / 'Paid parking runs along the Stanley Park seawall system; there is no parking directly at the beach itself.')
blocking.claim: "...there is no parking directly at the beach itself."
blocking.problem: This directly contradicts every other surface on this same page bundle, which repeatedly and specifically refer to 'Third Beach's parking lot' / 'the beach's own parking lot' as a real, named location (the site of the WWII soldiers' camp): composition.json's spike_statement ('the beach's parking lot was the soldiers' camp'), history.mdx ('on the ground that is now Third Beach's parking lot'; 'Visitors who park there today are parking on a wartime barracks site'), overview.mdx ('the beach's own parking lot'), and showcase.json's TEAHOUSE zone ('The Teahouse restaurant building and the adjoining parking lot'). travel.mdx's claim that parking exists only 'along the seawall system' and not 'directly at the beach' flatly conflicts with five other references to a specific on-site parking lot.
blocking.evidence: F21 (vancouvergunners.ca): "a soldiers' camp occupied the present third beach parking lot." F05 (Swim Guide) lists "pay parking on the stanley park seawall system" as an amenity of Third Beach itself, not a separate remote lot.
blocking.fix: Remove 'there is no parking directly at the beach itself' from travel.mdx and replace with something consistent with the rest of the page, e.g.: "Paid parking is available directly at Third Beach's own lot (part of the Stanley Park seawall parking system) — the same ground once occupied by the WWII battery's soldiers' camp."

advisory.where: history.mdx ('The war that justified the battery ended before the battery fired a shot at an actual enemy.'); showcase.json spike_explainer (twice: 'no battle was ever fought at Ferguson Point' and 'Ferguson Point was armed for war twice and fired on nothing; the guns' only recorded adversary was the city's own planning commission.')
advisory.claim: The battery never fired on an actual enemy / no battle was ever fought there.
advisory.problem: No fact in the research sheet confirms or denies whether the battery ever fired on an enemy. F14-F17 document construction, occupation, and stand-down but say nothing about combat activity. This is very plausibly true (no naval attack on Vancouver is otherwise documented) but is asserted three times as settled fact with no citation, which is exactly the kind of confident negative claim the audit is meant to catch.
advisory.evidence: No fact_id in research/third-beach-1.json addresses combat/firing activity at the battery.
advisory.fix: Soften to something like: "No source documents the battery ever firing on an enemy" rather than the flat declarative 'fired on nothing' / 'ended before...fired a shot' — or delete the claim if it can't be sourced.

advisory.where: history.mdx ('...long before any gun arrived, and still the legal basis for the parkland today.'); showcase.json spike_explainer ('The federal lease...is still the legal basis for the parkland today, a nominal-rent arrangement now well over a century old.')
advisory.claim: The 1887 federal lease is 'still the legal basis for the parkland today' (i.e., as of 2026).
advisory.problem: F25 is sourced to a 2015 Vancouver Gunners retrospective describing the historical lease; nothing in the fact sheet confirms the lease terms are unchanged or still in force as of 2026. Stating this as current fact extrapolates an 11-year-old source's description into a present-tense legal claim with no supporting citation.
advisory.evidence: F25 (vancouvergunners.ca, dated 2015): "this federally-owned land had been leased to the city for a nominal sum since 1887." Nothing addresses lease status past 2015.
advisory.fix: Hedge to past tense / as-documented, e.g.: "...a lease arrangement documented as still in effect as of the mid-2010s" or simply drop 'today' and 'still.'

advisory.where: history.mdx ('...even that connection isn't advertised on a sign for beachgoers to read.'); showcase.json spike_explainer ('There is no marker on Third Beach's own sand pointing this out... The sign, if there is one, is at the Teahouse, not the lot.')
advisory.claim: The Teahouse-officers'-mess connection isn't signposted for visitors.
advisory.problem: No fact in the sheet addresses on-site signage at the Teahouse or the beach; dead_ends explicitly notes 'No current Teahouse restaurant hours, menu, or operator name' is unconfirmed, but says nothing about signage either way. This is an unsourced negative claim, presented with confidence.
advisory.evidence: research/third-beach-1.json dead_ends list has no entry about signage; F23 only documents the historical building-use fact.
advisory.fix: Either remove the signage claim or hedge it as 'no source confirms any on-site signage explaining this history.'

advisory.where: showcase.json spike_explainer, 'Two accounts, one battery' section
advisory.claim: Vancouver Gunners is called "the most detailed contemporary account of the fort."
advisory.problem: 'Contemporary' normally means written at the time of the events (1930s-40s); the Vancouver Gunners source is dated 2015, a modern retrospective, not a contemporary record. Minor terminology error, not misleading about the facts themselves.
advisory.evidence: research/third-beach-1.json: F15-F17, F19-F22 all cite vancouvergunners.ca with date_of_source "2015".
advisory.fix: Replace 'contemporary account' with 'detailed retrospective account' or 'the most detailed surviving account.'
